column9: Rollback to a savepoint after upgrading a row lock must not lose the pre-savepoint conflict protection; the exact post-rollback lock strength is engine-specific.
column10: DEL-ISO-010/011/012 verify data/version rollback but not retained conflict protection after a savepoint lock upgrade.
column11: Pre-savepoint conflict protection across savepoint rollback is not directly proven.

column9: A child insert racing a parent primary-key update/delete must resolve with the correct FK or serialization outcome for the isolation level.
column10: DEL-FK-001..004 cover parent delete, crossed deletes, retry and snapshot visibility, but not parent primary-key movement.
column11: Primary-key update versus referencing insert is an uncovered FK concurrency schedule.

column9: Locking or deleting through an update chain must re-evaluate the newest row and distinguish key-changing from non-key-changing updates.
column10: DEL-TRAVERSAL-001/002/004 exercise update-delete chains, old secondary keys and READ COMMITTED stale-predicate re-evaluation.
column11: Core portable semantics are already covered; PostgreSQL advisory/key-share mechanics are not needed.

column9: A reader/locker traversing an update chain must not allow a concurrent key move/delete to produce stale-row effects.
column10: DEL-TRAVERSAL-003/004 prove stable old-version visibility and READ COMMITTED predicate refresh after concurrent key/value movement.
column11: Portable traversal semantics are already represented.

column9: MERGE WHEN MATCHED predicates must be rechecked against the current target row after a conflicting concurrent update.
column10: DEL-MERGE-001/002 cover a simple conflicting matched update and disjoint MERGE operations only.
column11: No DelosDB test proves concurrent re-evaluation of multiple WHEN MATCHED predicates.

column9: Concurrent DELETE/UPDATE/MERGE interactions must produce a serial result when MERGE contains MATCHED DELETE or key-changing UPDATE actions.
column10: Inherited MergeStatementTest covers MERGE DELETE syntax/functionality; DEL-MERGE-001/002 do not cover concurrent DELETE actions.
column11: Concurrent MERGE DELETE and delete-versus-merge schedules are unproven.

column9: Pruning/vacuum must retain versions and index reachability needed by an older live snapshot.
column10: MvccSqlLongReaderPurgeStressTest, MvccSqlVacuumTest, MvccRawStoreVacuumTest and ordered-index tests cover retained-reader purge/vacuum safety.
column11: The permanent-table horizon invariant is already a first-class DelosDB proof.

column9: Explicit VACUUM/ANALYZE commands obey PostgreSQL table-lock and ownership rules.
column10: DelosDB vacuum/purge is not exposed with PostgreSQL VACUUM/ANALYZE ownership semantics.
column11: The user-visible command and privilege contract is PostgreSQL-specific.

column9: Two serializable transactions that both observe absence and then insert the same unique key must distinguish serialization failure from an ordinary visible duplicate.
column10: DelosDB has unique enforcement and isolation tests, but no equivalent read-empty/read-empty/insert-same-key serializable schedule.
column11: Serializable uniqueness anomaly classification is not directly tested.

column9: Concurrent creation of a dependent object and dropping/altering its dependency must never leave dangling catalog references.
column10: DEL-DDL-001..004 cover table/index/trigger DDL serialization but not create-versus-drop dependency publication races.
column11: Adapt the invariant only to DelosDB-supported dependency pairs such as table/index/trigger/constraint.

column9: Inner, outer, natural, USING, aliasing and non-equi join result semantics.
column10: Inherited JoinTest/joins.sql/OuterJoinTest plus Stage 5C/D differential join generation already cover the portable surface.
column11: PostgreSQL-only row/JSON/operator extensions are outside the DelosDB SQL contract.

column9: Correlated/uncorrelated IN, EXISTS, scalar subqueries and nested subselect semantics.
column10: Inherited SubqueryTest, NestedWhereSubqueryTest, ExistsWithSubqueriesTest plus Stage 5C/D generated subqueries cover the portable surface.
column11: No broad import is justified; future individual gaps can be selected if fuzzing exposes one.

column9: Index creation, uniqueness, expressions/options and index-backed result correctness.
column10: Inherited index.sql/desc_index.sql/CreateIndex tests plus DelosDB ordered-index and DDL concurrency tests cover supported index semantics.
column11: PostgreSQL access methods/options are engine-specific.

column9: CHECK, UNIQUE, NOT NULL and constraint error behavior.
column10: Inherited Derby language/constraint suites and DelosDB unique/FK lifecycle tests already cover supported constraints.
column11: No uncovered portable family identified at inventory level.

column9: Functional MERGE matching, insert/update/delete actions and error cases.
column10: Inherited MergeStatementTest is extensive; Stage 4 adds basic concurrent MERGE.
column11: Only the separately inventoried concurrent recheck/delete schedules are gaps.

column9: Foreign-key creation, validation, cascades and functional error cases.
column10: Inherited foreignkey.sql/refActions plus DelosDB FK concurrency specifications cover the supported contract broadly.
column11: The specific parent-key update race is tracked separately as PG-002.

column9: Validate InnoDB index_merge/intersection/sort-union plans and guard against wrong results in those plan shapes.
column10: Stage 5 indexed/unindexed differential fuzzing already checks result equivalence under alternative DelosDB index choices.
column11: DelosDB does not expose MariaDB index_merge as a compatibility contract; plan-specific assertions are non-portable.

column9: Descending and mixed-direction indexes must return correct range/IN/group-min-max results.
column10: Inherited desc_index.sql, InListMultiProbeTest and aggregateOptimization.sql directly exercise descending indexes and range ordering.
column11: MariaDB optimizer-trace/index_merge details are non-portable.

column9: MIN/MAX with GROUP BY and composite indexes must preserve results across optimized and ordinary plans.
column10: Inherited aggregateOptimization.sql and Stage 5 grouped aggregate differential probes cover supported semantics.
column11: QUICK_GROUP_MIN_MAX_SELECT is MariaDB-specific implementation detail.

column9: Join reorder/plan choices must not change result semantics across complex predicates.
column10: Inherited Derby join optimizer tests plus Stage 5C/D generated joins/subqueries compare indexed and unindexed physical plans.
column11: Use as future reference only if a concrete DelosDB optimizer mismatch appears.

column9: A DELETE waiting behind primary-key updates must follow the current row and delete it exactly once after the writer commits.
column10: DEL-TRAVERSAL-001/002 prove delete-after-update and stale-key behavior across heap/MVCC.
column11: Portable semantic intent is already represented.

column9: A transaction selected as deadlock victim while resuming a previously granted lock must not continue as if a cancelled later lock were held.
column10: DEL-DEADLOCK-001..004 prove victim selection and rollback integrity but not grant/resume/cancel races inside a continuing scan/update.
column11: Post-victim wakeup correctness under a changing wait graph is unproven.

column9: Purge must remove obsolete secondary-index entries without leaving stale index state.
column10: MvccRawStoreVacuumTest, MvccSqlVacuumTest, MvccSqlLongReaderPurgeStressTest and ordered-index lifecycle tests cover DelosDB secondary-index purge safety.
column11: InnoDB page-layout/statistics checks are implementation-specific.

column9: Online index creation applies concurrent DML row logs correctly while purge is active.
column10: DEL-DDL-002 intentionally serializes DelosDB CREATE INDEX with active writers rather than using InnoDB online-DDL row logs.
column11: The upstream mechanism is outside DelosDB architecture; its end-state invariant is already covered by serialized index build tests.

column9: Crashes immediately before/after DDL metadata commit must recover to a wholly old or wholly new schema with usable data/indexes.
column10: MvccRawStoreUniqueLifecycleTest covers one unique-constraint crash boundary, and recovery suites cover WAL generally, but not a matrix of ALTER/CREATE INDEX DDL crash windows.
column11: General supported-DDL crash atomicity remains under-tested.

column9: Crash at group-commit/binlog phases must keep table state synchronized with MariaDB binary log state.
column10: DelosDB WAL crash/recovery tests cover database durability; it has no MariaDB binlog/group-commit compatibility contract.
column11: Binlog synchronization is MariaDB-specific.

column9: Foreign-key DDL, cascades, validation, rollback and restart behavior.
column10: Inherited Derby FK/refAction tests plus DEL-FK-001..004 and DelosDB recovery tests cover supported portable semantics.
column11: Select only concrete future gaps rather than importing this broad InnoDB suite.

column9: Avoid unnecessary InnoDB history fetches when checking secondary-record lock ownership.
column10: The upstream assertion is based on InnoDB buffer-pool read counters, not SQL semantics.
column11: Implementation/performance instrumentation does not map to DelosDB.

column9: READ COMMITTED page splits must not inherit InnoDB gap locks incorrectly during XA REPLACE operations.
column10: DelosDB does not use InnoDB next-key/gap-lock inheritance or this XA/page-split mechanism.
column11: The failure mechanism is storage-engine specific rather than a portable SQL semantic gap.

column9: DDL must finish consistently while concurrent transactions commit/rollback and purge observes their changes.
column10: DEL-DDL-002 plus rollback/vacuum/ordered-index tests prove the DelosDB serialized index-build and purge contract.
column11: MariaDB in-place ALTER row logging is not DelosDB architecture.

column9: A transaction upgrading a granted lock must interact correctly with already queued incompatible waiters and must not create avoidable/self deadlocks.
column10: DEL-DEADLOCK-002 covers two-reader conversion deadlock but not upgrade ordering when a third waiter is already queued.
column11: Queue-order/upgrade behavior around an existing waiter is not directly proven.

column9: Creating a unique index over duplicate values must reject the build without corrupting the table.
column10: Inherited Derby create/index tests and MvccRawStoreUniqueLifecycleTest cover unique-index creation and duplicate rejection.
column11: InnoDB prefix-index specifics are not portable.
